gloss: out of office; not in power; independent

definitions.gloss: out of office; in opposition; not in power
definitions.explanation: Being outside the ruling party or government. Used in politics to describe parties or politicians who are not currently in power.
Being outside of official or institutional organizations. Used for scholars, researchers, or professionals who work independently rather than within established institutions.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}で{負|ま}けて{在野|ざいや}に{下|くだ}った。
examples.english: They lost the election and went into opposition.

examples.japanese: {在野|ざいや}の{立場|たちば}から{政府|せいふ}を{批判|ひはん}する。
examples.english: To criticize the government from an opposition standpoint.

examples.japanese: {在野|ざいや}の{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}。
{大学|だいがく}に{属|ぞく}さず{在野|ざいや}で{研究|けんきゅう}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: They continue their research independently without belonging to a university.

examples.japanese: {在野|ざいや}の{歴史|れきし}{研究家|けんきゅうか}が{新|あたら}しい{史料|しりょう}を{発見|はっけん}した。
examples.english: An independent history researcher discovered new historical documents.

notes:
Literally means "being in the field" — i.e., among the common people rather than in the halls of power. Composed of {在|ざい} (being at) and {野|や} (field, the wild). The contrast is with {与党|よとう} (ruling party) in politics, or with institutional affiliation in academic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {在野|ざいや}{政党|せいとう}: opposition party
- {在野|ざいや}に{下|くだ}る: to go into opposition; to lose power
- {在野|ざいや}の{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}: independent researcher
- {在野|ざいや}{精神|せいしん}: spirit of independence (from established power)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {野党|やとう}: opposition party — the standard political term, more common
- {民間|みんかん}: private sector; civilian — broader, not specifically about opposition
- {無所属|むしょぞく}: unaffiliated; independent — specifically about organizational membership
- {与党|よとう}: ruling party
- {官|かん}: government; official sector
